agents.mandate: Fictional AI triage service of a fictional Abu Dhabi telehealth provider. System under test.
Health regulator for the emirate: patient safety, licensing of health services and oversight of AI in healthcare.
Telecommunications and digital government regulator: network outages, cloud and cyber incident coordination.
Data protection authority: personal data processing, breaches and cross-border transfers.
Answers questions from the other agents with cited clauses and global comparators. Does not decide.

payload.description: Three agents could not determine whether an automatic failover abroad is a transfer that needs prior approval, and the gate found no rule for ordering repatriation.

global_examples.how_it_handles: Provides a vital-interests derogation usable in emergencies.
global_examples.quote: A transfer to a third country may take place where the transfer is necessary in order to protect the vital interests of the data subject.

payload.implication: Providers cannot know in advance whether failover abroad is lawful; regulators decide case by case under time pressure.
payload.next_step: Check the primary text for an emergency-transfer route; if none, propose one tied to a notification duty.
payload.title: No rule covers emergency transfer of health data during cloud failover

payload.description: Isolating the backup region is required by a draft cyber rule and denied by the continuity-of-care rule; the gate escalated.
payload.implication: During a combined cyber and health incident there is no rule on which duty prevails.
payload.next_step: Ask DoH and TDRA which authority sets precedence; record the answer as a rule.
payload.title: Cyber containment conflicts with continuity of care
